blindSummary: This state/province combines high recorded lethality with legislative resistance. In the 2024 national count of violent deaths of LGBT+ people the federal capital led with 17, including 11 trans women, and this state/province followed directly behind the two leading jurisdictions. In March 2025 the state/province legislature voted down extending gender recognition to minors in open defiance of a national high-court ruling obliging states to provide recognition procedures - among the clearest cases of legislative refusal to implement the national documentation standard. Border-area reporting from a neighbouring state also documents rising attacks in municipalities on this state/province's frontier, with gay-men killings attributed to named municipalities there.

Report of an international human-rights organisation (6 March 2024): documents how the absence of any legal gender-recognition procedure in another state/province exposes trans people to police stops, denial of documents and institutional mistreatment - the clearest case in this country of what a state-level administrative gap does to trans residents and visitors.

A global news outlet's development report (24 July 2024): the capital criminalised transfeminicide with sentences of up to 70 years after the 2016 killing of a trans sex worker whose attacker was released despite footage and witnesses and remains at large; activists welcome the law as a watershed, while the reporting notes that convictions so far lag the statute's promise.
